name: HomeAssistant_inabox_v3
description: HomeAssistant_inabox installs Home Assistant OS as a virtual machine on your Unraid server through a short setup wizard - it does not run Home Assistant itself inside this container. Open this container's WebUI, pick a Home Assistant OS release and a few settings, and it creates the VM, downloads and attaches the disk, and hands you back a normal Unraid VM. Once a Home Assistant VM exists - whether this wizard created it or you already had one running - this container's WebUI becomes a small status panel instead of the wizard: it shows the VM's address, whether Home Assistant has answered there, and a Start button if the VM is stopped. If you stop or remove this container, the Home Assistant VM keeps running; it is managed by Unraid's own VM tab like any other virtual machine, not by this container. Keeping a VM running - an automatic restart if it stops unexpectedly, plus a notification - is opt-in per VM from the status panel and off by default; nothing is ever turned on for you. If you already run Home Assistant in a VM on this server, the wizard finds it by reading the VM's own disk rather than guessing from its name, and the status panel lists it alongside anything this container installs - there is no separate "adopt" step to click through. The wizard can also pass a USB device on this server through to the Home Assistant VM, for a Zigbee, Z-Wave or similar radio, and calls out devices it recognises as likely candidates rather than presenting a bare, unlabelled list. This needs direct access to your VM manager (libvirt), your Domains share, Docker's own socket and a handful of Unraid system paths in order to build and manage the VM correctly - that is expected and required, not a mistake in this template. It has no login of its own, so keep it on a trusted LAN rather than exposing it to the internet.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Where the wizard keeps its own state, downloaded Home Assistant OS images and the VM XML it generates. Safe to back up; deleting it just means starting the wizard over.

paths.name: Domains Share
paths.description: Your Unraid VMs share. This is where the wizard writes the Home Assistant OS virtual disk.

paths.name: Libvirt Socket
paths.description: Lets the wizard talk to Unraid's VM manager (libvirt) to create the Home Assistant VM and check on it. This is the folder libvirt creates its socket in, not the socket itself, so this container can start before or after the VM service without getting in its way. Required - do not change.

paths.name: Docker Socket
paths.description: Read-only access to Docker, used only to resolve this container's own host paths so the VM configuration the wizard writes points at real paths on your server. Required - do not change.

paths.name: VM Icons
paths.description: Where the Home Assistant icon is placed so it shows up next to the VM in Unraid's VM manager. Required - do not change.

paths.name: Domain Config
paths.description: Read-only access to Unraid's VM Manager settings, used to pick the correct default network for the new VM and to check up front whether Unraid will let a VM start at all. Required - do not change.

paths.name: QEMU Firmware
paths.description: Read-only access to Unraid's QEMU firmware files, used to copy the UEFI variables file the VM needs to boot. Required - do not change.

paths.name: Notifications
paths.description: Lets the wizard raise notifications that show up in the Unraid GUI, such as when setup finishes. Required - do not change.

paths.name: Emhttp Scripts
paths.description: Read-only access to Unraid's own web GUI scripts and state (including the state/var.ini file used to check the Unraid version and to exclude the boot flash drive from USB device selection, reached through Unraid's own internal symlink). Used to run Unraid's own notify script, so this container's notifications go out through whatever you have already configured - browser, email, or an agent such as Apprise - instead of only the notification bell. If this mount and 'Emhttp State' below are both absent, notifications fall back to the bell automatically; nothing breaks. Required - do not change.

paths.name: Emhttp State
paths.description: Read-only access to Unraid's own runtime state - nginx.ini, so a notification's link points at your server's real address. Also completes the 'Emhttp Scripts' mount above: Unraid's own emhttp/state path is a symlink onto this folder, and Unraid's notify script (and the boot-flash-identity read it enables) needs both mounts present together to resolve. Required - do not change.

paths.name: Notification Agents
paths.description: Read-only access to Unraid's own notification settings and the notification agent scripts you have configured there (for example, Apprise), so Unraid's own notify script can route this container's notifications the way you already set up rather than only to the notification bell. Disclosure: agent scripts in this folder carry their own credentials in plain text (an Apprise agent's Matrix username and password, a webhook URL, and so on) - this container only reads that folder to hand notifications to Unraid's own script and never transmits or logs its contents itself, but the credentials are exposed to this container, and to anything else with access to it, exactly as they already are to every other process on your server with read access to /boot. Required - do not change.

ports.name: WebUI
ports.description: Port the setup wizard's web page listens on. Open this in a browser to install Home Assistant. This is the wizard's own port, not Home Assistant's - the wizard links to Home Assistant from inside itself once the VM exists, on whichever port that VM turns out to answer on.

variables.name: HA_inabox version
variables.description: The version of this template, so the container can tell whether it matches the image running inside it. If Unraid ever updates this image to a new incompatible major version without also updating this template (templates do not update themselves), the mismatch is caught and explained on this container's WebUI instead of failing silently. Required - do not change.
